heroHeadline: Day 86 of Op Ghazab — UNAMA 'Grave Concern' Over Taliban Decree Permitting Child Marriage by Silence; 17-Day Strike Pause; Journalists Day 13–16 in Taliban Detention
heroSubtitle: On May 22, 2026 (Day 86 of Operation Ghazab lil-Haq), the UN Assistance Mission in Afghanistan (UNAMA) formally issued a statement expressing 'grave concern' over Taliban Supreme Leader Hibatullah Akhundzada's Decree No. 18, 'Code on Judicial Separation of Spouses,' which treats the silence of a 'virgin girl' as implicit consent to marriage — effectively enabling child marriage under Taliban law. The decree, published May 14, also requires women to pursue complex judicial avenues to separate from a spouse while men retain near-unilateral divorce rights. The Taliban's Ministry of Justice rejected UNAMA's characterization, stating the decree follows Islamic law. No new confirmed Pakistani cross-border airstrikes into Afghanistan since the May 5 Dangam (Kunar) strike — a 17-day pause — as Pakistan continues precision intelligence-based operations within Pakistani territory. On May 21 (Day 85), ISPR announced a 48-hour cumulative total of 23 Fitna al-Khawarij militants killed across IBOs in Datta Khel, Spinwam (including wanted commander Tor Saqib, Rs3M bounty), and Bannu, North Waziristan. Three journalists remain in Taliban detention: Paigard News Agency head Jawid Niazi (Day 16), TOLO News presenter Mansoor Niazi (Day 15), and political editor Imran Danish (Day 13). The Taliban's new family law (enacted May 18) and Decree No. 18 have drawn condemnation from over 100 international rights organizations. No formal ceasefire; no Urumqi Round 2 date announced; China silent on mediation since April 8.
footerNote: Data sourced from UNAMA, SIGAR, ACLED, Brown University Costs of War Project, US DoD, Reuters, BBC, Al Jazeera, Tolo News, Dawn, Geo News, HRW, OHCHR, OCHA, NPR
